title: Hybrid hot/scratch reservoir for fragment consolidation and interleaved prefill
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Problem: As more tenants run long-context models concurrently, small, interleaved KV fragments produce a high fragmentation overhead on GPU-resident paged attention caches. This increases prefill latency when fragments must be reassembled, drives frequent micro-evictions, and causes decode stalls during peak traffic. Existing approaches (LRU windows, simple slot coalescing) reduce some churn but do not address bursty interleaving and tenant hotspots.

Goal: Introduce a hybrid hot/scratch reservoir system and a low-cost consolidation pass to reduce fragment scatter, lower re-prefill rates, and improve decode p95 while preserving fairness across tenants. The system should: (1) keep a small, rapidly-accessible "hot" pool of pinned fragments for latency-critical slices, (2) maintain a larger, opportunistic "scratch" reservoir for short-lived or bursty fragments, and (3) run consolidation during low-util windows to coalesce tiny fragments into contiguous microsegments.

Success metrics: p95 decode latency reduction >= 10% on multi-tenant benchmarks; re-prefill requests reduced by >= 30% for 95th-percentile tenants; no more than 5% regression in overall throughput; GPU memory fragmentation score (internal metric) improved by >= 20%.

Design summary:
- Hot reservoir: small, tenant-weighted pinned region (per-node quota) for recently used prefixes and KV tails that show high reaccess probability. Pinning uses a probabilistic pin score that factors access recency, token frequency, and customer SLA weight.
- Scratch reservoir: a spill area for transient fragments using shorter residency TTLs and fast-path eviction. Scratch entries are allowed to be coalesced into microsegments when consolidation runs.
- Consolidation pass: background micro-coalescer that opportunistically merges adjacent small fragments belonging to the same model sharded segment. Runs only when GPU util < threshold (configurable) or during scheduled low-traffic windows. Consolidation uses a cheap two-pass algorithm to avoid long defragmentation pauses.
- Interleaved-prefill awareness: prefill scheduler will route requests to prefer hot-resident fragments; when a prefill must read many small fragments, scheduler can request a temporary "pin burst" in the scratch pool to avoid mid-decode eviction storms.
- Kernel interaction: add hints to kernel scheduler to co-locate prefill and decode tasks touching the same microsegment to reduce data movement and take advantage of warm L2/L1 caches.

Operational controls and safety: start with conservative pin quotas and short consolidation quotas. Expose per-tenant weight knobs and a global fragmentation guard that can pause consolidation if tail latency drifts. Track metrics and enable automatic rollback if p95 latency worsens beyond an SLO delta.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype in user-space allocator (no kernel changes) with tenants simulated in the perf harness. Validate basic pin scoring and scratch eviction policies. (Spike: 1 week)
2) Implement hot/scratch pools inside runtime allocator with persisted counters and counters exported to observability. Add lightweight consolidation daemon with soft rate limit. (2-3 weeks)
3) Integrate prefill scheduler hints and kernel-scheduler co-placement hooks (coord with kernel team). Add per-tenant quotas. (2 weeks)
4) Canary rollout on dedicated cluster group, run multi-tenant workloads and measure success metrics. Gradual enablement with feature flag. (2 weeks)

Testing and observability: build synthetic workload that mimics interleaved small-fragment access patterns (derived from production traces). Dashboards: fragmentation-score, re-prefill-rate, p50/p95 decode latency, consolidation-run-time, pinned-reservoir-occupancy, scratch-eviction-rate. Add debug endpoint to list microsegment mappings for an instance (read-only).

Risks and mitigations:
- Consolidation CPU/GPU overhead could increase tail latency: mitigate by rate limits and running only during low-util periods.
- Incorrect pinning could starve other tenants: use tenant-weight quotas and decay timers; expose emergency drain API.
- Hard-to-detect correctness bugs in coalescing microsegments: comprehensive unit tests and destructive fuzzing on allocator structures.

Notes: This ticket focuses on allocator-level design and runtime integration; separate follow-ups should address cross-node eviction coordination and long-term compaction strategies for on-disk snapshotting.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Spike complete: local perf harness shows prototype pin scoring reduces simulated re-prefill by ~38% on 16-tenant interleaved trace. Still seeing occasional consolidation stalls under 95% load; need rate-limiter.

2026-02-25 - Design review with Kernel team (notes in Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hybrid+Reservoir+Design. Kernel hooks required: task co-placement hint and soft prefetch hint. Kernel owners: Lena Cohen, Omar Singh.

2026-02-28 - PR opened for allocator prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/2345. Initial code contains hot/scratch pool structures and probabilistic pin scoring. Requesting early review from @lena and @kai.

2026-03-04 - Benchmarks on canary infra (node-group canary-3): p95 decode -14% vs baseline under mixed load; re-prefill rate -42% for top-10 tenants. Observed small increase (3%) in consolidation CPU time; acceptable within current limits.
2026-03-10 - UX/Console: added fragmentation-score metric to per-model dashboard prototype: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/kv/fragmentation. Need PM review about exposing pin quotas to customers.

2026-03-12 - QA found an edge-case where consolidation tried to merge fragments across model version boundaries leading to incorrect KV addresses. Hotfix: consolidation skips fragments with mismatched version headers. Follow-up: add unit test coverage and integration test with rolling model updates.

2026-03-14 - Next steps: finish kernel scheduler hints (blocking PR in kernel sync), add emergency drain API, extend canary to two more regions. Assigned follow-ups: ENG-198421 (emergency-drain-API), ENG-198422 (cross-node-eviction-prototype).
